# $\mathrm{SL}_n(F)$ is generated by the conjugates of the upper unitriangular matrices

Let $F$ be a field, $n \ge 1$, and $U_n(F)$ the group of upper unitriangular matrices of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $1$ on the diagonal and $0$ below it. Then $\mathrm{SL}_n(F)$ is the subgroup of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ generated by the conjugates $g U_n(F) g^{-1}$, $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)$.

Proof. Each conjugate of $U_n(F)$ lies in $\mathrm{SL}_n(F)$, which is normal, as unitriangular
matrices have determinant $1$. Conversely, an
[elementary transvection](../double-commutators-of-transvections/is-elementary-transvection.md)
$1 + a e_{ij}$ with $i < j$ lies in $U_n(F)$, and one with $i > j$ is $P (1 + a e_{ji}) P^{-1}$ for the
permutation matrix $P$ of the transposition of $i$ and $j$, whose $(j, i)$ entry is above the
diagonal; so every elementary transvection lies in a conjugate of $U_n(F)$, and these generate
$\mathrm{SL}_n(F)$ by [the generation by elementary transvections](generation-of-special-linear-groups-by-transvections.md).
